    "The study focuses on litter-to-litter variation and does not directly assess concordance with human clinical outcomes.",
    "The analysis of VPA studies is limited to whether experimental unit was correctly identified and good design features were mentioned, not the actual concordance of findings.",
    "The power analysis is based on specific parameters from one study (Mehta et al.) and may not be generalizable to all outcomes.",
    "The SOD1 mouse model example highlights translational failure but does not quantify concordance.",
    "The pharmaceutical industry's difficulty in reproducing published results is mentioned as a consequence of poor practices, but not as a direct measure of concordance."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": "The authors declare that they have no competing interests.",
  "key_numbers": [
    "9% (3/34) of studies correctly identified the experimental unit and thus made valid inferences from the data.",
    "14 studies (41%) it was not possible to determine the number of dams that were used (i.e. the sample size).",
    "4 studies (12%) the number of offspring used were not indicated.",
    "12% reported randomly assigning pregnant females to the VPA or control group.",
    "18% reported that the investigator was blind to the experimental condition when collecting the data.",
    "29% did not indicate whether both male and female offspring were used.",
    "61% reduction in residual variance when litter is taken into account for locomotor activity.",
    "50% reduction in residual variance when litter is taken into account for body weight.",
    "38% reduction in residual variance when litter is taken into account for marbles buried.",
    "35% reduction in residual variance when litter is taken into account for anxiety (open field).",
    "23% reduction in residual variance when litter is taken into account for grooming.",
    "A two-group study with three litters per group and eight animals per litter (48 animals) will have only a 30% chance of detecting the effect.",
    "A study with ten litters per group and one animal per litter (20 animals) will have almost 80% power.",
    "False positive rate is 20% rather than the assumed 5% if three 'treated' and three 'control' litters are used, with two offspring per litter.",
    "If the number of offspring per litter is 12 (total number of offspring = 72) then the false positive rate is 80%.",
    "Only 30% of papers in the behavioural neurotoxicology literature correctly accounted for litter effects.",
    "34% of papers in Developmental Psychobiology and 15% of papers in related journals correctly accounted for litter effects.",
    "Only 31% of studies reported randomly assigning animals to treatment conditions in the SOD1 mouse model of ALS.",
    "50% of papers in the neuroscience literature misinterpret interaction effects."
  ]
